reviewed_sources.authors: Sasha Brenner, Gaston Giribet and Luciano Montecchio
reviewed_sources.title: Symmetries of magnetized horizons
reviewed_sources.version: Published Physical Review D 103, 124006 (1 June 2021), nine PDF pages
reviewed_sources.read_scope: Title/abstract and Section VI, printed page 124006-8, equations (31)-(33) and the full cone-regularity/force discussion. The PDF page was also rendered and visually inspected.
reviewed_sources.use: Static magnetic Ernst metric and potential, and the established interpretation of its unequal axis deficits as the force needed to hold a magnetic monopole at rest. Our first-order metric, Maxwell and axis equations are independently calculated.
reviewed_sources.source_correction: The expanded azimuthal-period expressions printed after (33) do not equal the displayed Lambda squared at either pole. Direct substitution into (32) gives C_N=(1-BP/2)^4 and C_S=(1+BP/2)^4. The calculation uses those direct metric limits. This is not an OCR ambiguity: the printed page was inspected.
reviewed_sources.limits: The horizon charge formalism in Sections III-V and its proof dependencies were not audited or imported. The exact solution-generating theorem is established background, not newly independently proved here.

reviewed_sources.title: Rotating charged black holes accelerated by an electric field
reviewed_sources.version: arXiv:1006.4072v1, archive stamp 21 June 2010; six PDF pages; the manuscript header separately prints August 13, 2018
reviewed_sources.read_scope: Main text Sections I-IV, including the factored charged C-metric (2)-(8), projection and Harrison transformations (11)-(20), and both-axis regularity conditions (25)-(30).
reviewed_sources.use: Established acceleration-field equilibrium and elementary-flatness test. We specialize to the nonrotating magnetic dual with an explicitly declared orientation and geometric field normalization. The local first-order field equations and cone factors are independently verified rather than importing rotating formulas unaltered.
reviewed_sources.limits: The rotating solution and upstream projection/Harrison existence proofs were not independently reconstructed. The book and Ernst 1976 dependencies remain outside this scoped proof review. Our full nonlinear check is restricted to angular cone geometry; the independent bulk calculation is first order.

reviewed_sources.authors: Juan Maldacena, Alexey Milekhin and Fedor Popov
reviewed_sources.title: Traversable wormholes in four dimensions
reviewed_sources.read_scope: Complete Section 6.1 and subsections 6.1.1-6.1.4, including orbital frequency, naive and screened orbital drift, leading radiation, Unruh-like scale and thermodynamic qualification.
reviewed_sources.use: Established orbital support proposal and leading frequency, drift and radiation comparators. We retain g explicitly, impose the selected g^2=q^-2 family, and independently derive the resulting constants and exponents.
reviewed_sources.limits: Appendix G screening and circular-motion radiation/temperature dependencies are not newly proof-reviewed. Passing the naive unscreened scale diagnostic does not derive the actual field-line return. The local throat excitation scale is not a uniform gap of the exterior continuum; no adiabatic theorem, vacuum construction or physical stability is inferred.

access_notes: Attempted arXiv HTML views for the two older articles returned errors; exact PDF artifacts were obtained through INSPIRE and arXiv and retained in the ignored cache.
Both source-download sessions were polled by their live handles and completed with exit code zero. Neither was restarted on a timeout.
development_notes: The first verifier run passed all background/linear bulk equations and then failed the expected frozen-metric residual coefficient. Independent radial differentiation gives -2 B P^2/r^2 because the potential includes B/2; the initial expectation had a factor of two error. The expectation was corrected without relaxing any tolerance.
The static source's printed period expansion was checked against both the metric and the rendered original PDF; the direct metric limit was retained.
novelty_decision: Continue physical long-return damping with matched finite-duration band transfer as fallback. The local l=1 classical mouth response must include force balance. A globally static unsupported mouth is not supplied by this Ernst branch; the existing static calculation remains an auxiliary reference pending a controlled comparison. The selected weak-coupling family passes leading orbital, unscreened-drift and total-radiation hierarchies. These reproduce established mechanisms, not a new physical endpoint.
